source: Generated by emulator/build_tables_view.py from recovered/calibration/* and the findings reports for dumps/VIP_2A03.ori (SHA-256 82c2832024feae3d5427df4baddbaedcc80cdd0958e3e33155f4b78e1c21c2c0); names, units and uncertainty are the research's own.

conventions.addresses: rom_address / table_address are ROM offsets (load base 0), six hex digits. RAM addresses are five hex digits (F8xxx); multi-byte values are big-endian.
conventions.cells: Raw unsigned integers exactly as stored. Cell k (row-major) is at rom_address + k*cell_stride, cell_bytes wide. If cell_signed, reinterpret as two's complement first. Physical = raw*cell_scale + cell_offset in cell_unit; an empty cell_unit means no engineering unit is established (cell_label carries the research's own label).
conventions.table_address: Start of the table block (count byte or rows/cols header); rom_address is the first cell.
conventions.axis: raw = breakpoints as stored; values = the same in 'unit' when the research establishes a (nominal) scale, else a copy of raw with unit ''. Axes read from ROM also give rom_address/rom_bytes/rom_stride. Index axes (0..n-1) have none.
conventions.live: live_address is the RAM variable the firmware loads for that axis at the lookup call (empty if not a single direct RAM load at every call site; live_evidence says why). Read live_size bytes, divide by live_divisor, then interpolate that number over live_values to get a fractional position along the axis. live_kind: 'raw' = same domain as raw breakpoints; 'raw_rounded_high_byte' = firmware uses the rounded high byte of the word; 'grid_coordinate' = normalized 0..255 coordinate, node i sits at i*256/(n-1) and 255 only approaches the last node; 'index' = direct array index. source_* on a grid axis is the un-normalized variable behind the coordinate.
conventions.lookup: interpolate = count-prefixed X/Y curve (029D40 family); step = staircase band table (022492); index = direct array index; grid = rows/cols grid (029E26 / 029EB2).
conventions.scalars: raw is the unsigned ROM value; value is raw in 'unit' (nominal) or the signed/raw value when unit is ''. headline marks the values a driver or tuner would look for first.
conventions.nominal: All engineering values are nominal conversions from the firmware's own arithmetic (rpm word/8, temperature raw-64, MAP raw*105/256 kPa, spark raw/2); nothing was measured on a vehicle.
